title: Enterprise Account Executive (London)
descriptionHtml:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

Replit is experiencing extraordinary demand and seeking an Enterprise Account Executive with strong communication skills to drive our hyper-growth. Candidates with SaaS experience, particularly with some technical background (i.e. having some coding knowledge or prior experience at other developer tool companies) are ideal.

This full-cycle sales position encompasses new client acquisition. We believe this role offers a distinctive opportunity for people who excel in client-facing situations and have a passion for driving sales and AI. You'll leverage your skills to effectively communicate Replit's value proposition: a world where anyone can create software using natural language.

In this role you will:

  • Evangelize a future where anyone can create software in natural language, ushering in a change in the nature of the firm on par with the PC era

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for prospects and customers, guiding them through the buying journey

  • Conduct compelling product demonstrations and help realize the art of the possible by orchestrating non-engineering hackathons

  • Articulate Replit's value proposition and align it with customers' business objectives

  • Collaborate with product and engineering teams to ensure technical accuracy and successful delivery

  • Prepare tailored quotes and skillfully negotiate deals

  • Maintain accurate customer and forecasting data in Replit’s CRM (Hubspot)

  • Foster strong relationships with existing clients while identifying opportunities for expanded adoption

  • Optimize customers' use of the Replit platform through ongoing collaboration and support

  • Gather and communicate valuable customer feedback, championing their interests within Replit


Required skills and experience:

  • Experience in AE or SE/technical sales role, preferably in SaaS or developer tools

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Proven track record of meeting or exceeding sales quotas

  • Experience with, or direct observations of full-cycle sales, from prospecting to closing deals to managing existing customers

  • Proficiency in using CRM systems and sales tools (e.g., Hubspot)

  • Ability to quickly learn and articulate the value of new technologies

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think on your feet

  • Self-motivated with excellent time management and organizational skills

  • Passion for technology and staying current with industry trends

  • Experience with or strong interest in AI and machine learning is a plus

  • Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time for client meetings and events

Nice to have:

  • You're an active Replit user

  • You've worked at an early-stage startup or in developer tools

  • Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)

Tools + Tech Stack for this role:

  • Replit

  • Hubspot CRM

  • ZoomInfo

  • Clay

  • SmartLead

  • LinkedIn Sales Navigator

  • Hashboard, Hex

This role may not be a fit if:

  • You’re not based in London area

  • You lack an understanding of the software development lifecycle; have little to no coding knowledge

  • You’re not passionate about AI

  • You don’t enjoy being in client facing roles where 80% of your day is talking to others


Note: This role will begin as remote, with plans to transition to a hybrid model once we establish a local office presence.

Full-Time Employee Benefits Include:

title: Enterprise Account Executive
descriptionHtml:
SingleStore is looking for an accomplished sales professional to join our Sales Team. AI is moving from experimentation into production, and this role is an opportunity to break into AI while doing meaningful enterprise selling.

As an Account Executive, AI Hunter, your job is simple: create new SingleStore customers. You will find companies building AI applications where data access, real-time context, memory, retrieval, or operational scale is becoming a constraint—and turn those challenges into new SingleStore customers. You will own a broad territory, build a majority self-sourced pipeline, create demand in an emerging category, and close greenfield enterprise opportunities.

This is a true hunting role. You will engage customers before they have a defined project, develop customer-specific points of view, create urgency around business and technical problems, work with technical experts to land first production workloads, and build a measurable new-logo business with broad ownership. The ideal candidate is a measurable enterprise hunter who is competitive, curious, technically credible, resilient, and able to sell business outcomes. Direct AI sales experience is valuable, but proven selling ability and technical curiosity matter more than a narrow “AI seller” title.

Role and Responsibilities

  • Build and execute a territory strategy for net-new customer acquisition.
  • Prospect fearlessly across a broad account universe using proactive, persistent outbound, account-based, partner, and market-education motions; stay resilient and effective through rejection and ambiguity.
  • Form account hypotheses, map the buying center, and earn first meetings with relevant points of view tailored to the customer.
  • Engage executive, business, technical, security, and procurement stakeholders.
  • Lead great business-first discovery, connect AI and data challenges to fundable goals, and build quantified ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases.
  • Build and develop champions, multi-thread the buying group, earn executive and economic-buyer access, and maintain stakeholder alignment; own the stakeholder plan, mutual action plan, close plan, value case, stage gates, forecast, and commercial outcome.
  • Lead complex sales cycles through technical validation, security, legal, procurement, negotiation, and close.
  • Partner with Solutions and Forward Deployment Engineers and cross-functional teams to validate technical fit and establish the first production workload.
  • Navigate competitive displacement and maintain disciplined activity management, CRM hygiene, reporting, qualification, forecasting, and opportunity management; showcase clear metrics such as pipeline created, meetings, conversion, quota attainment, and new-logo performance.
  • Be AI fluent: use AI and research tools productively and responsibly while applying judgment, validating outputs, and separating facts from hypotheses.
  • Travel within the assigned territory as required. 

Required Skills and Experience

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying B2B enterprise software sales experience, ideally selling to large or technically sophisticated organizations; experience in data, cloud, analytics, AI, or adjacent technical domains is a plus.
  • Repeated, quantified quota success with clear ownership of new-logo wins and self-sourced pipeline.
  • Experience closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals involving executives, technical evaluators, security, legal, finance, procurement, and partners.
  • Ability to sell measurable business outcomes and build ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases.
  • Technical fluency in an adjacent domain such as databases, data infrastructure, analytics, AI/ML, cloud, Kubernetes, developer tools, cybersecurity, observability, or open-source software.
  • Strong qualification, account planning, forecasting, CRM, negotiation, and deal-management skills.
  • Learning velocity and coachability, demonstrated through specific behavior change after feedback; ability to explain technical concepts clearly to technical and executive audiences.
  • Executive presence, customer trust, resilience, intellectual honesty, and excellent communication skills.
  • B.A., B.S. degree or equivalent in a related field.
  • Experience with Fortune 500 or security-sensitive organizations, cloud ecosystems, open-source or consumption-based products, or emerging categories is preferred.

To all recruitment agencies: SingleStore does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to SingleStore employees. SingleStore is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with the Company.

SingleStore values individuals for their unique skills and experiences, and we’re proud to offer roles in a variety of locations across the United States. Salary is based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location, and is just one part of our total compensation and benefits package. Certain roles are also eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases and annual bonuses.

SingleStore’s salary range for this role is [£140,000 - £230,000]

title: Enterprise Account Executive (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
About Speexx: 

Speexx is the #1 platform for people development. Combining cutting-edge AI technology with world-class coaches, Speexx delivers digital business coaching and language training services for global workforces. Since 2012, Speexx has helped over 1500 international clients level up their organization's professional development and received over 200 prestigious accolades from top tier publications like G2, Fosway, and TIME Magazine for our best-in-class product. Together with our diverse network of trainers, coaches, and full-time Speexxies, we are building the future of learning and development, and this is just the start.  

We are looking for an Enterprise Account Executive based in France. However, we are also open to candidates located elsewhere in Germany, Spain, or Italy.

Your Impact

As Enterprise Account Executive, you will be responsible for driving new business growth by identifying, developing and winning strategic national and international accounts. Your role goes beyond generating new business: you will build relationships with key decision-makers, understand their business and People & Development priorities, and position Speexx as a strategic partner in addressing their skills development challenges. You will combine a strong acquisition mindset with a consultative approach, engaging prospects around their business challenges and building relevant, value-driven solutions. Working closely with Marketing, Business Developer, Customer Success and other internal teams, you will manage opportunities from initial engagement through to closing and ensure a strong transition of newly acquired customers into their long-term journey with Speexx.

What You'll Do

  • Identify, develop and win new strategic national and international accounts.
  • Build and manage a strong pipeline of qualified opportunities, aligned with acquisition and revenue targets.
  • Develop relationships with key decision-makers and stakeholders, positioning Speexx as a trusted and consultative business partner.
  • Develop a deep understanding of prospects' business, People & Development and skills development priorities and translate them into relevant value propositions using Speexx solutions.
  • Lead the full sales cycle, from initial engagement and qualification through solution development, negotiation and closing.
  • Manage complex, high-value opportunities involving multiple stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Lead commercial discussions and negotiations, including large and strategic deals.
  • Manage and contribute to RFP processes.
  • Collaborate closely with Marketing and Business developer teams to identify target accounts, generate demand and develop new opportunities.
  • Work closely with Customer Success and Growth teams to ensure a smooth handover of newly acquired customers and create strong foundations for their long-term development.
  • Monitor pipeline and forecasts, ensuring clear and accurate visibility through the CRM.
  • Represent Speexx as a strategic People Development partner in the market and contribute to the continued development of our business.

What You'll Bring

  • Strong experience in new business development and strategic B2B sales, ideally within a SaaS or technology environment.
  • Proven ability to identify, develop and win new strategic accounts.
  • Experience managing complex sales cycles and high-value commercial opportunities from prospecting through to closing.
  • Strong negotiation and closing skills combined with a consultative and solution-oriented sales approach.
  • Ability to understand prospects' business and People & Development challenges and connect them with relevant solutions and measurable value.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and confidence engaging with different stakeholders, including senior decision makers.
  • A proactive, entrepreneurial and results-driven mindset, with a strong ability to open doors, create opportunities and develop new business.
  • Experience with tender and RFP processes.
  • Ability to work effectively across teams in an international and fast-paced environment.
  • Fluency in French and English is required; additional languages are an advantage.
  • Strong proficiency in CRM and productivity tools.
  • Mastering AI

What We Offer

✨ International and collaborative environment with colleagues across Europe and Asia

✨ Continuous learning through Speexx Academy, mentoring programs, workshops, and external training

✨ Free access to world-class language training plus discounts for friends and family

✨ And because we operate across multiple countries, additional local benefits, including health & wellbeing support, mobility programs, and other country-specific perks, may apply depending on your location

Don't meet every requirement? We'd still love to hear from you. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply. Your unique experience and perspective might be exactly what we're looking for.

title: Enterprise Account Executive
descriptionHtml:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Disclaimer: We're open to hire Account Executives across our Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes and Biarritz offices.

⭐️ The Enterprise Account Executive job

We’re expanding our Sales team in France and are looking for a ‘full-stack’ Enterprise Sales to engage with prospects and turn them into happy Alan customers. You will join a team that mostly focuses on large companies from Tech, Syntec, HCR, and B2B services, interacting with everyone from HR executives to CEOs.

Why is this segment interesting?

  • Diverse workforce: Mix of 60% cadres / 40% non-cadres, often with subsidiaries or multi-site operations, ranging from highly tech-savvy employees to those requiring digital adoption support.

  • Critical challenges: Multi-stakeholder decision processes involving HRD, CFO, CEO, Payroll, CSE, Legal, Purchasing, Comp & Ben, Accounting, Brokers (creating multiple potential blockers), long sales cycles (multi-year conversations), RFP processes requiring deep audits and product customization, and strong influence from unions/CSE who can co-manage health insurance topics;

  • Company profiles: Flagship companies (widely known brands), groups with standalone entities or subsidiaries, often with focus on employee wellbeing (QVT programs, Great Place to Work), modern company culture, and strategic communication about digitization or employer brand attractiveness;

  • HR priorities: Increasing productivity, obtaining fair and competitive pricing, contributing to employee well-being through customized health plans, simplifying HR processes with digital platforms, and managing change management concerns when implementing new health insurance (biggest fear for large companies)

  • Critical business characteristics: This segment requires breadth & depth of expertise to navigate complex organizations, account-based strategies with Key Account Management approach, early engagement in company roadmaps, face-to-face meetings, co-creation of insurance and digital products (tailored offers considering past results, specific regimes, demographics, payroll system integration), and ability to work through RFPs and with brokers. Sales cycles are volatile with high stakes: 1 deal = 50% of annual target for Enterprise AEs.

Our approach for Enterprise companies positions Alan as a strategic partner in health rather than just an insurance provider, emphasizing our digital platform for fluid UX, customized health plans at fair pricing, and health/well-being services. Success requires leveraging high-level connections, building professional materials, and potentially creating exclusive "Health Clubs" or labels for early adopters.

What will you do with us?

You’ll own the entire sales cycle, from prospecting to closing. In our Enterprise Sales team, you will deal with companies with more than 300 employees, including all CAC40 companies.

At Alan, Account Executives drive deals and close strategic opportunities with prospects. We sometimes handle some customer relationships to ensure the best possible onboarding. You’ll educate prospects, provide inspiring product demos, and onboard key stakeholders, making the transition from prospect to customer seamless.

We expect you to understand and apply the Alan Smart & Soft selling method. This method ensures the prospect experience is an integral part of the overall Alan customer experience—making it pleasant and delightful for everyone. We expect you to be instructive to prospects (Smart), as well as to define the best personalized high-touch strategy that suits best each prospect (Soft).

You’ll also help us grow and improve as a company, challenging us to enhance our product(s), methods, and strategy, and getting involved in initiatives to expand our customer base.

Take a look at this testimonial from Emilie Quellec and watch Julien Plessis, both part of the Enterprise Sales team 👀


⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

You’ll be a great fit for the Enterprise team at Alan if you:

  • Have at least 8 years of experience in Sales, including at least 2 years managing the whole Enterprise Sales cycle, from prospecting to closing.

  • Have full working proficiency in French (C2 and above) and an advanced level in English.

  • Are highly organized with exceptional follow-up skills;

  • Have empathy and are passionate about understanding and solving prospects' problems;

  • Can influence through persuasion, negotiation, and consensus-building;

  • Have a deep understanding of value drivers in recurring revenue business models;

  • Have a great attitude and ability to collaborate in a small team;

  • Are eager to learn fast and make an impact from day 1;

  • Are based in (or willing to relocate to) Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the D-F level range.

If you're still wondering whether this could be the best move for you, take a look at this article from Lucie Leflour, our Sales Lead in France.


Everything else is a plus. We care about having a diversity of experiences, profiles and backgrounds in our team.


🙌 Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer:

  • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary, for permanent contracts only.

  • Flexible office with hybrid setup. Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or sponsored co-working hubs in Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

  • All the tools you need. Top of the range equipment: Macbook Air, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

  • Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only).

  • Transport. Generous transit benefit

title: Environmental Test Laboratory Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As Validation Laboratory Module Lead, you build Harmattan's environmental test laboratory from a blank page and then run it. Today too much of our environmental testing depends on external labs and their scheduling, which slows our development down as much as it costs us. Your mission is to change that, and you own it end to end: defining the capabilities we need, specifying and buying the machines, contributing to the choice of premises, recruiting and leading the technicians, and drawing the line between what we bring in-house and what stays external.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership role, and the lab does not exist yet. Beyond building it, you become the Group's reference on environmental testing: supporting the validation teams on the lab validation of their projects, reviewing the environmental parts of their test plans, and handing our test procedures over to the quality team as products move into production.

What you'll do

  • Define the lab and select the equipment: Establish the capabilities we need, then specify, evaluate and procure the machines, covering climatic and thermal cycling, water and dust ingress, vibration and UV ageing, including a large climate room in which we can fly a drone under controlled wind and temperature.

  • Decide what we internalise and what stays external: Draw the line between the tests worth owning and those better bought from external labs, such as accredited qualification or rare capital-heavy tests, and revisit that line as our product range grows.

  • Set up the facility: Contribute to the choice of premises, then take the site from layout and utilities through to installation, safety and commissioning.

  • Build and lead the team: Recruit and lead a team of two to three lab technicians, set the working standards, and grow the team's capability as the lab ramps up.

  • Support the validation teams: Assist the validation modules on the lab validation of their projects, and peer-review the environmental sections of their test plans, making sure the right tests, conditions and acceptance criteria are defined.

  • Hand over to production: Work with the quality team to transfer our test procedures as products reach PVT and mass production, so that production-line testing stays consistent with what validation defined.

What we're looking for

  • At least 10 years in environmental testing, including setting up or substantially developing a test lab. This is a senior role and we are looking for depth, not a first lab job.

  • Strong command of environmental test methods and the equipment behind them: climatic and thermal cycling, vibration, water and dust ingress, UV, and the standards that frame them.

  • Proven equipment judgement: able to specify, evaluate and procure test machines, and to argue build-versus-buy and in-house-versus-external on both cost and technical merit.

  • Experience leading a small technical team, or clear readiness to step into that responsibility.

  • A rigorous, methodical approach to test planning, acceptance criteria and documentation.

  • Comfortable working across functions with engineering, validation and quality, and translating between them.

  • Engineering degree in a relevant field (mechanical, materials, electronics, physics or similar), or equivalent experience.

  • Bonus: experience with defence or aerospace test standards (MIL-STD-810, RTCA DO-160 or similar); familiarity with lab accreditation and metrological traceability such as ISO/IEC 17025; a background in drones or robotics.

  • Working-level English; French is a plus.

  • Based at our Paris-area site, with occasional travel to our Swiss site.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Flight Structures Test Engineer
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Flight Structures Test Engineer to plan, build, and execute the component and structural tests that prove our hardware is ready to fly.

Test is where analysis meets reality. Your data will qualify our hardware, validate our models, and give the team the evidence needed to make the next design decision. You will work closely with structural analysis, mechanical design, manufacturing, and the workshop to develop reliable test setups and high-quality results.

About us

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, have just crossed €10m in revenue for our first operating year and are applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

  • Plan and execute structural and component tests, including proof, burst, and mechanical-load testing.

  • Design and build test setups, fixtures, and load-introduction systems with the design and workshop teams.

  • Instrument test articles with strain gauges, pressure sensors, displacement sensors, and other measurement systems.

  • Set up data acquisition, process and evaluate test data, and correlate results with structural analysis.

  • Write test plans, procedures, reports, and technical documentation that hold up to review.

  • Help build structural-test capability from the ground up, including safety procedures for pressurised testing.

What we are looking for

  • A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline.

  • First hands-on experience in structural or component testing through industry, research, or a student engineering team.

  • Practical understanding of strain gauges, sensors, instrumentation, and data-acquisition systems.

  • A safety-conscious and structured approach, combined with a willingness to work hands-on with hardware and test equipment.

  • Fluent English and the ability to document technical work clearly.

Desirable experience

  • Hydrostatic or pneumatic pressure testing.

  • Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for test-data processing and evaluation.

  • Data-acquisition systems, test-bench automation, or test-facility development.

  • Working proficiency in German.

Benefits and important information:

  • We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent.

  • Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success.

  • Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas.

  • Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday

  • Free access to shared company housing

Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week.

We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger.

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.
  • Work independently to troubleshoot integration and flight-readiness issues while collaborating cross-functionally with hardware engineering, firmware/software teams, operations, and QC engineering to escalate complex challenges when required.
  • Act as the primary technical authority in customer engagements, translating mission requirements into concrete system architectures and demonstrable solutions built on AuterionOS and Skynode.
  • Participate in flight testing activities to validate platform stability, safety, and mission performance, resolving technical issues often directly in the field during customer trials and demonstrations.
  • Contribute to technical documentation and continuous improvement of engineering processes.
  • Feed customer and market requirements back into product and engineering teams to influence the roadmap of the Auterion stack.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Degree in Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace or Robotics Engineering, or a related field
  • Working proficiency in C/C++ and Python: you can read, debug and patch existing code and write small tools and scripts
  • Comfortable in Linux environments, including the command line, logs, Docker and basic networking (IP, TCP/UDP)

  • Structured troubleshooting: you can isolate whether a problem is software, hardware, configuration or RF, often under time pressure in the field

  • Willing to travel and work on-site with customers, including at test ranges and in field environments

Nice-to-have

title: Founder's Associate – Praktikum / Intern (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Deine Rolle

Die Steuerberatung steht vor ihrer größten Umwälzung seit Jahrzehnten: Nachfolgewelle, Konsolidierung, technologischer Bruch. Die meisten Studierenden lesen darüber in Fallstudien. Hier sitzt du an dem Tisch, an dem entschieden wird.

Vogel berät mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen in steuerlichen, kaufmännischen und strategischen Fragen. Darauf bauen wir eine Beratungsplattform für den deutschen Mittelstand, organisch und durch Zukäufe, mit einem gemeinsamen Setup, in das jede neue Einheit integriert wird. Vogel ist inhabergeführt, und du arbeitest unmittelbar an den Themen der Geschäftsführung mit.

Du studierst im fortgeschrittenen Bachelor oder im Master oder bist im Gap Year. Die Fachrichtung ist zweitrangig, wichtig ist, dass du herausgestochen bist. Du willst kein Traineeprogramm mit festen Stationen, sondern wissen, wie Entscheidungen tatsächlich entstehen: mit unvollständigen Daten, unter Zeitdruck, zwischen Menschen unterschiedlicher Meinung.

Das Praktikum dauert drei bis sechs Monate in Vollzeit. Du verantwortest ein bis zwei eigene Themen und arbeitest direkt mit der Geschäftsführung.

Deine Verantwortung

Analyse und Entscheidungsvorlagen

  • Du nimmst eine offene Frage der Geschäftsführung, strukturierst sie und lieferst eine Antwort auf zwei Seiten, mit eigener Einschätzung. Dein Maßstab: Wer die Vorlage liest, kann danach entscheiden.

  • Du baust Auswertungen aus unseren Zahlen: Ergebnisse je Einheit, Mandatsstrukturen, Auslastung, Wachstumstreiber. Die Daten holst du selbst, deine Annahmen dokumentierst du mit.

  • Du prüfst Annahmen nach, die im Haus als gesetzt gelten, und stellst sachlich fest, wenn etwas nicht mehr stimmt.

Eigene Themen von der Frage bis zum Ergebnis

  • Du übernimmst eigene Themen über die gesamte Strecke und trägst die Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

  • Du arbeitest in laufenden Vorhaben quer durch das Unternehmen mit: Integration eines zugekauften Hauses, Aufbau eines neuen Beratungsfelds, Einführung eines Werkzeugs in allen Einheiten.

Interne Steuerung und Kultur

  • Du baust an den Formaten mit, über die das Unternehmen gesteuert wird: Berichtswege, Kennzahlen, Entscheidungsvorlagen, interne Kommunikation.

  • Du verantwortest Anlässe, an denen unsere Kultur konkret wird, von der Town Hall bis zum Sommerfest, gemeinsam mit dem Growth-Team.

  • Du wirkst im Recruiting mit: Sichtung, eigene Einschätzung zu Kandidaten, Mitarbeit am Bewerbungsprozess.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 3 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du hast zwei eigene Themen von der Fragestellung bis zum Ergebnis verantwortet und selbst vorgetragen.

  • Mehrere deiner Entscheidungsvorlagen haben zu tatsächlichen Entscheidungen geführt.

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du verantwortest ein eigenes, abgegrenztes Thema, bei dem die Geschäftsführung nicht mehr nachfasst.

  • Die Bereichsleitungen sprechen dich direkt an, wenn sie eine Analyse brauchen.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Du siehst in wenigen Monaten, wie ein wachsendes Unternehmen entscheidet, und nimmst eine Arbeitsweise mit, die in jeder späteren Rolle trägt. Wer überzeugt, bleibt im Gespräch.

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Ein fortgeschrittener Bachelor oder Master mit sehr guten Leistungen: Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Jura, Naturwissenschaften oder ein Fach, in dem du nachweislich herausgestochen bist.

  • Erste Praxis in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld ist ein Plus: Beratung, Investment Banking, Private Equity, Scale-up, Founders Office oder eine eigene Gründung.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber Denkschärfe und Umsetzungskraft mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du schreibst klar und knapp. Zwei gute Seiten schlagen bei uns zwanzig vollständige.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Recherche, Analyse und Drafting. Repetitive Aufgaben sind für dich ein Anlass zur Automatisierung.

  • Bei einer offen formulierten Aufgabe machst du deine Annahmen explizit, schlägst eine Richtung ein und justierst unterwegs.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du verträgst die direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung: schnelle Iteration, hohe Eigenständigkeit und auch Aufgaben, die nicht im Lebenslauf glänzen.

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Die Steuerberaterin mit 20 Jahren Erfahrung weiß Dinge über ihr Mandat, die in keinem Modell stehen.

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keine Konzern-Strategieabteilung. Was du schreibst, geht in eine Entscheidung, die diese Woche fällt.

  • Keinen Elfenbeinturm. Eine Empfehlung ohne Verantwortung für die Umsetzung ist hier keine Lieferung.

  • Kein Praktikum mit Rotationsplan. Du bekommst eigene Themen und damit auch die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen.

  • Keine Zuarbeit für eine Zwischenebene. Du trägst deine Ergebnisse selbst vor der Geschäftsführung vor.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

title: Founding Design Engineer | CodeSpeak
descriptionHtml:
Role: Founding Design Engineer (Senior / Staff)

Company: CodeSpeak

Location: London, on-site. Ideally you already live in London. Candidates based elsewhere are welcome to apply, and remote is possible for a very strong candidate, but UK-based candidates come first. Candidates with a Global Talent visa, granted or in process, are a good fit.

Job Type: Full-time

About CodeSpeak

Agents write more code every month. Human brains stay the same. CodeSpeak is building a program model that sits one level above code, so people can see how a program works and changes over time without reading much of it. The goal is to give control back to the developer: you think about architecture, and the routine goes away.

CodeSpeak was founded by Andrey Breslav, the creator of Kotlin, which millions of developers use daily. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. When it comes to program analysis and developer tooling, these are some of the best people in the world. CodeSpeak is backed by Accel and by funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, and funding covers several years.

Here is the open problem. The team has a fair idea of what the program model should look like. It does not yet know how to visualise it. As Founding Design Engineer you will decide how it looks, then build it and ship it. The core engineering team has just been hired, and nobody on it has design-engineering skills. You are the missing piece.

CodeSpeak is a UK company. It has no business in Russia and no ties to Russian companies. It is still testing which problems it can solve best, so priorities may shift.

What you are expected to do:

Design and delivery

  • Own how people interact with CodeSpeak: in the CLI, on the web and on any future platform.

  • Design the interfaces yourself. Build many prototypes, decide on the right UX and ship the result.

  • Harden the prototypes users liked, so they hold up on real data, with the same care for performance and product quality as for design.

  • Ship features to production without help from the rest of the team.

Product problems

CodeSpeak works with unusually complex information: developer intent, requirements, code, architecture, the relationships between them, how they change over time, contradictions and dependencies. The job is not to display it, but to help developers understand it, navigate it and act on it.

  • Find a way to visualise CodeSpeak's new, higher-level program model.

  • In your first 30 days, visualise the architecture of a codebase split into components. Go deeper from there: a single component, its diff and its code review.

  • Then interfaces that let developers navigate structured requirements and how they relate to each other, review requirements alongside code review, see how requirements map onto parts of the codebase, explore how intent, architecture and code change over time, browse agent sessions, find contradictions between requirements, and edit and reorganise requirements rather than only view them.

  • Web UI is the simplest and most obvious platform. Some of this will live in the console. VS Code plugins and other desktop frameworks may follow, and the final scope is still open.

Ways of working

  • Find tasks and clarify requirements without waiting for a brief. Nobody will micromanage you. Egor and Andrey give general direction.

  • Work directly with the founder and the engineering team to turn early ideas and hypotheses into intuitive, interactive product experiences.

  • Take part in design meetings, where many decisions are made on the spot.

  • Explain and defend your design decisions to Egor and Andrey. Both hold strong opinions, and both argue hard.

  • Argue for your tasks, and step back with good grace if the team disagrees.

What you need to succeed:

Craft

  • You can design an interface, prototype it and ship it to production on your own.

  • You have strong design taste, and your portfolio shows it: UX, interaction design, information architecture and visual hierarchy. For this role the portfolio is critical.

  • You make complex information or a complex data model easy to read. Think maps with metadata or dense dashboards, with non-trivial state. Tools that read and write count for more than infographics or landing pages.

  • You have solid computer science and software engineering fundamentals, plus TypeScript, and deep experience building production apps with modern UI frameworks such as React. At least 3 years of delivering production software.

  • You understand the problems of engineers, because engineers are CodeSpeak's users.

How you work

  • You can say why you made each design choice. "I'm an artist, I see it this way" will not work here.

  • You are curious and self-directed, and you care about making programming better. You gather requirements and find projects yourself.

  • You actively improve your own workflow with AI-powered coding tools.

  • You work hard and can be reached when a task needs it. The team has no weekend-work culture.

  • You think fast and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You speak Russian, which is the team's working language. This is a priority, not a hard rule, and a strong candidate without Russian will still be considered.

Nice to have

  • A background as a frontend engineer with good taste. Engineers from SwiftUI, desktop, mobile or full-stack are welcome if they visualise complex things very well.

  • Experience with complex data visualisation.

  • Some sense of what an early-stage startup is like. A big-tech engineer who knows what they are joining can fit, and so can a former co-founder.

A technical degree is not required. Self-taught people and people with degrees in geology or biology have done well in roles like this.

What you get:

  • An unsolved problem with real room for your taste. The team is inventing a new way to represent programs, and you decide how it looks.

  • A boutique team of strong engineers, built carefully, who have built developer tools at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph and Elastic.

  • An ML team of four, led by Emeli Dral. She co-founded Evidently, an evals startup, and co-authored a very popular Coursera course for data scientists.

  • Day-to-day work with Egor, Andrey and the tech lead.

  • Backing from Accel and from funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, with funding for several years.

  • A UK contract with a pension and medical insurance.

  • Autonomy. You set your own tasks and nobody hovers over you.

  • Work in AI, a field most people want to be in.

title: Founding Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The Role

This is Dust's first PM hire. You'll work closely with the product team, turning raw GTM signal, company priorities, and user feedback into well-formed problems the team can act on.

What you will change:

  • A lot of product signal doesn't reach the team in an actionable shape today. You'll create and run the process that connects signal to shaping to prioritization.

  • Implementing company strategies across functions requires ownership and orchestration. You'll translate company priorities into an intelligible, trackable set of product, marketing, and operations initiatives.

  • You'll enrich prioritized projects with distilled business and user context and market perspective so that the people building them make better decisions.

Our designers and engineers stay close to product decisions from conception to delivery. You're here to make their context richer and their priorities sharper. You enable distributed ownership, you don't replace it.

What You'll Do

  • Qualify and synthesize feedback: Sit at the intersection of GTM, users, and product. Turn high-volume, unstructured input into a small set of well-framed problems worth solving.

  • Shape initiatives: Work with engineers and designers to translate validated problems into initiatives ready for Stack Rank — with clear objectives, KPIs, and scope.

  • Drive outcome tracking: Own reporting on whether what shipped actually moved the needle. Feed that back into the next round of decisions.

  • Improve internal coordination: Connect Marketing, Comms, GTM, and Product — reduce the friction that slows things down when multiple functions need to move together.

  • Own outcomes, not outputs: For cross-functional initiatives, you'll own the goal — objectives, KPIs, orchestration, reporting.

  • Own artefacts in the Dust platform (agents, skills, data, etc..) to continuously rewire and augment the above for yourself and the team

What You Can Expect

Team

Dust is a growing team of about a 100 people. Most of the product and engineering team is based in Paris, with close collaboration across our teams in New York, San Francisco, and London.

The interview process

The process is designed to understand how you think, collaborate, and operate in an ambiguous, technical environment:

  • Recruiter conversation: motivation, background, logistics, and fit for an early-stage environment.

  • Hiring DRI conversation: discussion with a senior member of the product team.

  • Product exercise: collaboration exercise based on a real company priority.

  • Founder conversation: discussion with one of our founders on product judgment, attitude, and ability to operate with distributed authority.

  • Onsite: working sessions with members of Engineering, Design, and GTM. We’ll look at how you gather context, identify the important problems, collaborate on possible approaches, and leave ownership with the people closest to the work.

We care more about the quality of your reasoning and collaboration than about arriving at a predetermined answer.

What We're Looking For

  • Founding PM mentality: Senior individual contributor and builder balancing capacity to build the practice in the company while being hands-on.

  • 5–8+ years of product experience, including time at an early-stage company where you had to build process from scratch.

  • Genuine product taste. You know great from good in the world of tech products, and you bring deep perspective, judgment and conviction to any preferences you voice.

  • Excellent information synthesis skills, distilling a messy pile of customer feedback, sales calls, and Slack threads into sharp problems.

  • Technical proficiency earn the respect of engineers. You don't need to code, but you understand systems and tradeoffs easily deeply.

  • Builder mindset at heart. You use AI tools fluently and you're excited about what they unlock for how PMs operate. You've thrived in environments where everyone is a builder and you want to strengthen that.

  • Effective communication. You'd rather say one clear thing than three vague things.

  • Comfort with distributed authority. You influence by being right, not by being in charge.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

title: Founding Research Engineer or Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
About Grubel

Grubel is a research lab that builds AI for high-stakes knowledge work, starting with law. Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. General-purpose AI applies the same system to every legal matter, varying only what goes into a limited context window.

To meet the depth and diversity of legal work, we let every matter build its own AI: engineer the right data for the matter, adapt the model and agent to it, and track what improves. We combine the three into a matter-specific improvement loop that runs until the system delivers what the matter demands.

Grubel was founded in 2026 by Moritz Hardt, director at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and formerly a UC Berkeley professor and Google Brain researcher; and Reinhard Heckel, professor of machine learning at the Technical University of Munich, on leave to build Grubel. The founding team includes engineers with PhDs in computer science and experience in foundation-model pretraining at Mistral and legal AI research at Thomson Reuters. The lab has offices in Munich and Tübingen.

Point Nine led an oversubscribed pre-seed funding round with backing from leading AI researchers and founders, including Jeff Dean, Chris Ré, Ion Stoica, and Harvey co-founders Gabe Pereyra and Winston Weinberg.


About the role

We are looking for a Founding Research Engineer or Research Scientist to develop the methods and systems that make matter-specific AI possible. You will work on data curation, agent environment design, model adaptation, training, and evaluation. We do not draw a sharp boundary between research and engineering: everyone contributes substantial code, owns experiments end-to-end, builds systems, and helps turn successful methods into products. Research is empirical and engineering intensive.

You will work directly with Grubel’s founders, engineers, legal experts, and enterprise partners. As an early member of the team, you will also help shape Grubel’s technical direction and research culture.

What you’ll work on

  • Developing, testing, and evaluating methods for adapting models and agents to individual legal matters

  • Designing benchmarks and evaluation tasks for complex legal capabilities

  • Developing data curation strategies for scaling from evaluation tasks to training tasks

  • Building infrastructure for training, inference, experimentation, and evaluation

  • Working with legal experts and enterprise partners to turn legal workflows into agentic workflows

  • Turning successful research methods into reliable product capabilities

You may be a good fit if

  • You hold a master’s degree or PhD in machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or a related field, or have equivalent research or industry experience

  • You have either a strong machine-learning research record or significant experience building large-scale machine-learning systems

  • You have trained and evaluated language models or built agentic systems

  • You are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable owning technically ambiguous problems

  • You are curious about how legal work actually gets done and enjoy working with domain experts

Particularly relevant experience

Any of the following would be valuable, but we do not expect candidates to have all of them:

  • LLM post-training, fine-tuning, or reinforcement learning experience

  • Data curation, synthetic data, or human-in-the-loop data generation pipelines

  • Evaluation harnesses and benchmark development

  • Distributed training, inference, or experiment infrastructure

  • Publications, open-source contributions, or deployed research systems

  • Legal AI or another expert-intensive application domain

Logistics

  • Munich or Tübingen. We value working together in person, prefer candidates based near one of our offices, and expect at least one day per week in the office. We plan to establish a Zurich office in 2027.

  • Full time employment

  • Competitive salary plus a stock option grant in Grubel, Inc., our US parent company.

title: Frontend Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

 

Role

As a Web Frontend Engineer, you will build the core web experiences, including Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

You will own complex, highly interactive product surfaces from architecture through implementation, working closely with product, design, backend and AI engineers to make AI a native part of how users communicate, write, organise and work.

 

What You'll Own

  • Build major web experiences across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs, and Sheets.

  • Develop complex interactions including real-time messaging, collaborative editing, rich-text editing, scheduling, tables, and spreadsheets.

  • Build reusable frontend architecture and components that work consistently across ActAI applications.

  • Integrate streaming AI responses, proactive actions, and model-driven experiences directly into product workflows.

  • Own frontend performance, responsiveness, reliability and accessibility across browsers and devices.

  • Work closely with product and design to take ideas from prototype to production quickly.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Strong experience building complex, production web applications using React, TypeScript and modern frontend technologies.

  • Deep understanding of frontend architecture, state management, browser APIs, and performance.

  • Experience building highly interactive products such as chat, collaboration, productivity, document editing, calendars, or workspaces.

  • Experience with real-time systems, WebSockets, streaming APIs, or collaborative interfaces.

  • Strong product and UI judgment with attention to interaction details.

  • Able to independently own features from technical design through production.

 

Outcomes

  • Users can communicate, write, organise and collaborate seamlessly across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

  • Complex interactions such as group messaging, editing, scheduling and collaboration feel fast and reliable.

  • AI capabilities are integrated naturally into product workflows rather than added as separate chatbot experiences.

  • Frontend architecture remains fast, maintainable and reusable as ActAI expands into new applications and workflows.

 

Tech Stack

  • TypeScript

  • React.js / Next.js

  • HTML / CSS

  • WebSockets / streaming APIs

  • Node.js

  • REST / GraphQL APIs

 

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world-class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively and move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high-quality work and learning.

Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment and execute independently. Our goal is to put in the hands of our users a truly magical product.

 

Interview Process

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews.

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us and help bring practical AI benefits to billions of users globally.

title: Genesis-World: Core Simulation Engine Engineer
descriptionHtml:
What we’re building

Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.

Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.

Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.

This is at the core of Genesis AI’s strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.

Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.

You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.

The problems waiting for you

  • Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.

  • Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.

  • Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.

  • Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.

  • Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.

  • Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.

  • Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.

  • Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.

  • Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.

Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.

Who you are

You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design.

You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job.

  • Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc).

  • Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale.

  • Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants.

  • At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon)

  • Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community.

Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work.

title: Group Creative Director Automotive (w/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Wir suchen am Standort München eine:n Group Creative Director Automotive (w/m/d) zur kreativen Führung und Weiterentwicklung eines unserer größten internationalen Automotive-Accounts. Die Rolle ist zunächst auf 18 Monate befristet.

Wir sind eine globale, socially-led Creative Agency mit über 1.300 Mitarbeitenden in 17 Büros weltweit. In einer Welt, in der Social Media Kultur prägt, helfen wir Marken dabei, Ideen zu entwickeln, über die Menschen sprechen.

Wir verstehen Online-Communities, Kulturen und Subkulturen über die gesamte Social Landscape hinweg. Zu unseren Kund:innen in Deutschland zählen unter anderem AUDI AG, Mercedes-Benz Trucks und Müller. We Are Social ist Teil der Plus Company.

Als Group Creative Director übernimmst du die übergeordnete kreative Verantwortung für einen unserer größten internationalen Accounts. Du entwickelst eine klare kreative Vision, setzt Standards und stellst sicher, dass unsere Arbeit über unterschiedliche Kampagnen und Workstreams hinweg überzeugt.

Dabei leitest du kreative Führungskräfte und Teams, gibst Orientierung und förderst Eigenständigkeit und Ownership. Du behältst das kreative Gesamtbild im Blick, setzt entscheidende Impulse und steigst dort tiefer ein, wo deine Erfahrung den größten Unterschied macht. Außerdem vertrittst du den kreativen Output der Teams gegenüber der Kund:innen und stehst ihnen als Sparringspartner zur Seite.

Requirements

Was beinhaltet die Rolle?

  • Übergeordnete kreative Verantwortung für einen internationalen Automotive-Account sowie Entwicklung und Umsetzung einer klaren kreativen Vision
  • Führung und Weiterentwicklung kreativer Führungskräfte und Teams mit dem Ziel, Eigenständigkeit, Ownership und kreative Exzellenz nachhaltig zu stärken
  • Sicherstellung einer hohen kreativen Qualität über unterschiedliche Kampagnen und Workstreams hinweg
  • Konzeptionelle Führung bei großen Kampagnen, Pitches und kreativen Schlüsselprojekten – mit einem klaren Fokus auf innovative, kulturell relevante Social-First-Ideen
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Client Service, Strategy, Media und Production, um kreative und strategische Potenziale bestmöglich auszuschöpfen
  • Aufbau und Pflege vertrauensvoller Beziehungen zu Senior Stakeholder auf Kund:innenseite sowie überzeugende Präsentation und Vertretung kreativer Ideen
  • Proaktive Identifikation kreativer Wachstumschancen und Weiterentwicklung des Kunden durch neue Ideen, Formate und innovative Ansätze
  • Aktive Mitgestaltung der kreativen Standards und Weiterentwicklung von We Are Social über den eigenen Account hinaus

Wonach suchen wir?

  • Langjährige Erfahrung in einer seniorigen kreativen Führungsrolle auf Agenturseite sowie in der Entwicklung großer, integrierter und Social-First-Kampagnen
  • Automotive-Erfahrung und ein gutes Verständnis für die Markenführung und Strukturen großer internationaler Automobilmarken
  • Herausragende Konzeptstärke, strategisches Denken und ein tiefes Verständnis für Social Media, Plattform-Mechaniken und kulturelle Trends
  • Nachweisliche Erfahrung in der Führung und Weiterentwicklung kreativer Teams sowie die Fähigkeit, Verantwortung zu delegieren und Eigenständigkeit zu fördern
  • Souveränität und Überzeugungskraft im Umgang mit Senior Stakeholder sowie exzellente Präsentations- und Pitch-Fähigkeiten
  • Entscheidungsstärke, ein ausgeprägtes Ownership-Mindset und die Fähigkeit, auch bei hoher Komplexität Prioritäten zu setzen und kreative Orientierung zu geben
  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse

Benefits

Warum du Teil unseres Teams werden solltest?

Lebendiger Teamgeist: Wir tragen das Adjektiv social sehr bewusst im Namen und leben einen starken Teamgeist und eine offene Unternehmenskultur mit flachen Hierarchien, in denen deine Stimme zählt!

Spannende Projekte mit internationaler Reichweite: Wir arbeiten an digitalen Projekten, die Maßstäbe setzen! Unsere Kund:innen kommen aus dem B2C- und B2B-Umfeld und sind sowohl lokale als auch internationale Player.

Global verbunden und lokal verwurzelt: Unsere Teams an den Standorten München und Kreuzberg profitieren von einem nachhaltigen Wissensaustausch mit den WAS Standorten weltweit und sind im Glockenbachviertel und Kreuzberg zu Hause.

Flexibilität - Yes please!: Hybrides Arbeiten vereint für uns die Vorteile des Home Offices mit denen des Arbeitens im Büro. Genau deswegen haben wir uns für einen 2/3 Split entschieden, der bedeutet, dass wir bei 40h mindestens 2 Tage vor Ort mit unseren Kolleg:innen und 3 Tage im Home Office arbeiten. But that’s not all! Darüber hinaus sind wir große Fans von Remote Arbeit. Deswegen hast du bei uns die Möglichkeit 20 Tage innerhalb Deutschlands und weitere 20 Tage innerhalb Europas remote zu arbeiten. Wenn du also kein großer Fan des Deutschen Winters bist, join us und du kannst diese Zeit in Portugal oder Griechenland genießen.

Mehr Benefits für dich: Weil wir wissen, wie wichtig Well-being ist und wir Benefits einfach lieben, bieten wir dir mehr als nur den Standard. Genieße 2 zusätzliche Health Days, Menstrual Leave, einen freien Tag an deinem Geburtstag, eine Kooperation mit Wellpass, das Deutschlandticket, eine Mitgliedschaft bei OpenUp und vieles mehr.

title: GTM
descriptionHtml:
About Nomos

Europe pays more than twice as much for electricity as the US or Asia. To reach competitive price levels, Europe has to lean on solar and deliver the flexibility that makes this feasible. Nomos is building a full-stack power company to unlock that flexibility by connecting millions of homes to Europe’s energy markets.

At Nomos, we care about our craft and take full responsibility for what we build. We hire for spikes, not an absence of weaknesses, and look for exceptional ability backed by a record of achievement. This has brought together IMO and IOI medalists, former founders and Olympic athletes in a team whose individual strengths reinforce one another.

 

What you’ll do

Nomos is built on the trust of our partners and the households we serve. Our partners put their reputation behind the energy products we build together. You will earn that trust with new partners and build our go-to-market function.

  • Identify lighthouse manufacturers, installers, and emerging companies with innovative products, proven demand, and loyal customers.

  • Lead the sales cycle and high-stakes negotiations with global businesses, including publicly listed companies.

  • Build and maintain a qualified pipeline, with clear priorities and next steps for every opportunity.

 

Exciting challenges

  • Build the playbook. Develop a repeatable approach to winning partnerships and scaling our go-to-market. Pair it with unreasonable hospitality: recognise when a partner needs more, go the extra mile, and follow through on the details.

  • Understand the market, not just the deal. Think ahead about how technologies and partner needs are evolving. Work with product, engineering, and partner success to shape what we build and where we grow.

 

Who you are

  • You have the ability to go deep. You showcased that you can understand the product and market better than a customer in a very short time.

  • You bring warmth and presence. You put people at ease, listen before you speak, and pay attention to the details that matter to them.

  • German and English, both fluent. You’re comfortable leading a negotiation in either.

 

References

Anne Roellgen

 

Why join us?

As an early member of Nomos, you’ll help shape the company and share in its financial upside. Backed by Index Ventures, we’re building a European category leader in one of the world’s largest industries, making electricity affordable and Europe more competitive.

Building a power company from scratch brings complex, rewarding challenges and the chance to solve Europe’s energy crisis for the long term. You’ll learn from people with exceptional depth in their fields, challenge each other’s thinking and take responsibility from the start.
