title: GTM Lead Germany
descriptionHtml:
At Parallel, we build AI agents to help healthcare facilities automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.


Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost in manual, repetitive administrative work. Legacy software hasn’t helped, it’s made things slower, more complex, and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change that. Our technology combines Large Language Models with system-level automation to handle real work inside existing hospital tools. No integrations, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding workflows and frees up time for medical staff to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024, are backed by top investors (Index, Frst, Y Combinator, Hexa, Kima Ventures, Better Angle), and we’re just getting started.

 

The future of healthcare isn’t just digital — it’s automated. Come help us build it !

Context

Germany is one of Europe's largest healthcare markets, and its hospitals face the same pressure we solve in France: rising administrative load, staff shortages and revenue lost to incomplete coding.

As Germany GTM Lead, you are our first hire in the country. You will report directly to Paul Lafforgue, CEO and co-founder, and work closely with Chris, our CTO, and the product team in Paris. You will own everything from the first prospecting call to the first signed contracts, shape the local product and build the German team from zero.

  • Location: 2 to 3 months of onboarding in Paris, then based in Germany with regular trips to Paris. Office in Munich or Berlin.

  • Team: none at first. Around 5 people in H1 2027, around 12 by the end of 2027.

Your mission

Take Parallel from zero to a validated, repeatable market in Germany by the end of 2027: 2 to 3 flagship hospitals as paying customers, 2M€ ARR and a local team of around 15.

Outcomes

  • First customers: build the pipeline with Paul, book your own first meetings (your calendar starts empty), sign the first pilots and turn them into paying contracts.

  • German go-to-market: pick the segment to win first (private groups, public or university hospitals), adapt the pitch to the German healthcare context, test our success-based pricing, including in public tenders, and build visibility through networks, trade shows and customer references.

  • Local product: run the feedback loop between German hospitals and the product & tech team, and bring in local medical expert(s) to validate usage

  • German team: hire a team growing from 0 to around 12 across sales, ops, engineers and set up the office.

  • Growth story: report on Germany's progress to the leadership team and investors, and, if we acquire a local company, contribute to due diligence and lead the integration of the acquired team.

Who you are

A builder who wants to open a market, not run one. This job is for you if:

  • You are a native German speaker, with your schooling and career in Germany, and fluent in English, our working language with headquarters.

  • You have 5 to 10 years of experience, including at least 2 years in a quota-carrying B2B sales role.

  • You have lived at least one 0-to-1 experience: you founded a company, joined a startup of fewer than 50 people or launched a new market.

  • You enjoy being on the ground: meeting customers, travelling and opening doors yourself.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and an empty playbook.

  • You are credible with hospital leadership (CEO, CFO, chief medical officer) as well as with physicians.

  • You can convince first hires to join a company that nobody in Germany knows yet.

  • You are open to about 3 months of regular trips to Paris, with a long-term base in Germany.

  • Bonus: you know the German healthcare system, or you have already launched a business.

  • Bonus: you have hired and managed a team, or worked on M&A or the integration of an acquired team.

Our values

  • Play to Win: we are not here just to participate, ship something “good enough”, or enjoy the startup ride. We want to win. That means caring deeply about outcomes, moving fast and being willing to put in the intensity required when it matters.

  • High Trust, High Standards: trust is our default. If you joined us, it's because we believe you can own your scope and make good decisions. We don't want a company built on approvals, control and micromanagement. But trust comes with responsibility. The more freedom we give, the higher the standard we expect.

  • Low Ego, Hands-On: no one at Parallel is above doing the work. Titles, seniority and past achievements don't exempt anyone from getting their hands dirty. Everyone should be willing to step into the arena when needed. Leadership means taking responsibility, not creating distance from execution.

  • Don't Take Yourself Too Seriously: we are extremely serious about our mission. We don't need to be extremely serious about ourselves. Building a company is intense. We want Parallel to remain a place where people enjoy spending time together, laugh, celebrate and bring energy to the people around them. High standards and good vibes are not opposites. We want both.

Hiring process

  1. Screening call (40 min)

  2. Practical case + Q&A with Paul, CEO (video call, 45 min)

  3. Presentation of your written practical case (video call, 1h30)

  4. Business case in Paris (half a day)

Why should you join us?

  • A rare opportunity: open Parallel's first international market as employee #1 in the country, with a direct line to the CEO and the room to build the team, the playbook and the office your way.

  • A product that already works: you start with a live product, around 800 customer references in France and local CTO in Germany ready to adapt it with you.

  • Real-world impact: every hospital you sign gives clinical staff time back from paperwork to improve patient care.

  • Package & perks: competitive salary and meaningful equity, health insurance, top-quality equipment and a public-transport contribution.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

title: GTM Lead, UK - SMB/MM/Enterprise
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The Role

We’re hiring a hands-on sales leader for the UK. You’ll build, lead, and coach the regional Sales team, deliver against ARR and pipeline goals, and build a repeatable local growth engine.

You'll act as the business lead for your market, with accountability for revenue. As a sales leader, you'll lead and coach the sales team, stay close to customers and deals, and build a repeatable sales approach that fits your market. As an orchestrator, you'll coordinate the local pipeline generation activities that feed your number, including marketing and pre-sales. You'll work closely with leaders across BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Solutions Engineering, Deployment, and Customer Success, and influence how they support your market's priorities.

What you’ll do

  • Own the region’s ARR plan, forecast, and qualified pipeline. Work with the CRO to set priorities, understand capacity needs, and support the team to deliver against the plan.

  • Build and lead the regional Sales team. Hire, onboard, coach, and develop sellers, while staying hands-on in priority opportunities from prospecting and discovery through qualification, evaluation, negotiation, and close.

  • Make clear, evidence-based recommendations to Product based on regional customer conversations, deal patterns, and market needs. Build and refine a repeatable regional sales approach using pipeline, win/loss learning, and customer outcomes.

  • Drive the plan in partnership with field marketing to set priorities for events, campaigns, customer advocacy and community programs, and direct how field marketing resources are used to support your pipeline and ARR goals.

  • Partner with the marketing leadership, who own field marketing standards, methods and team management, to make sure regional programs are well executed, measured and consistent with Dust's broader marketing approach

  • Partner with BDR and Growth leaders to build a qualified pipeline through a deliberate mix of outbound and other locally effective channels.

  • Set direction for how Partnerships can support regional priorities. Work with the Partnerships lead to identify opportunities for sourcing, co-selling, or delivery.

  • Coordinate with Solutions Engineering, Deployment, Professional Services, and Customer Success to support credible evaluations, successful implementations, customer outcomes, and expansion.

  • Represent regional customer needs internally and share market learning with the CRO and functional leaders, contributing to consistent GTM practices across Dust.

Market-specific focus

United Kingdom

Build on early customer and partner traction. Use customer referrals, targeted events, and focused market experiments to build qualified pipeline and strengthen local customer proof.

What we’re looking for

  • A proven sales professional who has grown from individual contributor into people leadership, with 5+ years leading B2B software sales and coaching regional sales teams and a hands-on understanding of how to help reps succeed in-market.

  • You've owned a market or segment revenue number end to end, not just a team's quota. You've built pipeline through functions you didn't manage, such as marketing, partners and pre-sales, and you've made real calls about where capacity and budget go, including between direct sales and partners

  • Ability to lead by example in priority opportunities, from discovery through close.

  • Experience building pipeline and customer relationships in a market where the brand or sales motion is still developing.

  • A disciplined approach to forecasting and performance feedback, paired with high EQ and a genuinely supportive leadership style.

  • An appetite for building, testing, and refining a market over multiple quarters while balancing near-term results with durable growth.

What success looks like

The region delivers against its ARR and pipeline goals while developing a repeatable sales approach suited to local customers. The team builds customer trust and referenceable outcomes, cross-functional support is focused on regional priorities, and market learning informs Dust’s broader GTM approach.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

title: Head of EMEA Sales
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Founding Sales Leader in EMEA to build our business in the region from the ground up. We already have EMEA customers and real demand — today it’s served from the US. You’ll be our first person on the ground in London, and your job is to localize that business and turn it into a region.

This is a founding-leader role, not inheriting a machine. You’ll be in deals directly while making your first hires, with a mandate to scale the EMEA team to 20+ people this year across front-line leaders and sellers.

The right person for this role is a player-coach who has managed managers, sold to technical buyers, and hired quickly — and who wants to run a region before a bigger company would hand them one. If you’re energized by ambiguity, an unformed market, and building with what’s in front of you, this is one of the most consequential GTM roles at Baseten.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own EMEA: all segments, all markets, top to bottom.

  • Build the team. Recruit, hire, and onboard 20+ people this year, including the front-line leaders who will run it with you.

  • Carry the number. Build pipeline, run deals, and close business yourself while the team is coming together.

  • Establish our presence in the region — the London footprint, our reputation with EMEA buyers, and the local playbook for how enterprise buying works here.

  • Adapt the motion. Take what works in AMER and tune it to how technical buyers in EMEA actually evaluate and purchase infrastructure.

  • Partner closely with a US-based org across Sales, Marketing, Revenue Operations, Solutions, and Recruiting, with significant US timezone overlap.

  • Set the bar for execution, forecasting rigor, and speed as the region scales.

REQUIREMENTS

  • A proven hiring track record. You’ve built teams quickly and hired leaders, not just ICs, and you can point to the people you’ve developed.

  • Second-line leadership experience. You’ve managed managers and owned a multi-team org.

  • Enterprise selling experience against a technical line of business. You can hold your own with engineering and infrastructure buyers and want to go deeper on inference.

  • Scrappiness. You’re comfortable being the only Baseten person in the region on day one — building pipeline, closing deals, and recruiting at the same time, without the bells and whistles.

  • EMEA fluency. You know the regional markets and how enterprise buying differs from the US.

  • Comfort in a fast-moving, high-intensity environment. Here, that means you Slack faster than you talk.

  • A builder’s mentality. You own problems and their solutions, and you’re at your best in high-change, unstructured environments.

 

BENEFITS

  • Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

  • (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

  • Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

  • Paid parental leave

  • Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

  • (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

  • Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

Unser Portfolio umfasst eine breite Palette innovativer Systeme, die eine zuverlässige Produkthandhabung, eine stabile Linienleistung sowie eine effiziente Verbindung zwischen Verarbeitungs- und Verpackungsprozessen gewährleisten. descriptionHtml:

Innerhalb von nur drei Jahren sind wir auf 10 Standorte und mehr als 50.000 Kunden gewachsen. Damit gehören wir zu den am schnellsten wachsenden Unternehmen im Bereich der ästhetischen Medizin in Deutschland.

Und wir stehen erst am Anfang.

In den kommenden Jahren wollen wir unseren Wachstumskurs deutlich beschleunigen und MY HEALTH&BEAUTY als die führende Marke für ästhetische Medizin und Longevity etablieren.

Unser Erfolgsmodell basiert auf einem klaren Anspruch: höchste medizinische Qualität ohne Kompromisse zugänglich für Alle.

Unsere Behandlungen werden ausschließlich von Ärzten durchgeführt. Wir arbeiten mit den hochwertigsten Produkten führender Hersteller und setzen auf standardisierte Prozesse, intensive Schulungen und eine konsequent hohe Behandlungs- und Servicequalität.

Unser Ziel ist nicht der kurzfristige "Verkauf" einzelner Behandlungen, sondern der Aufbau langfristiger Kundenbeziehungen durch Qualität, Vertrauen und ein konstant exzellentes Kundenerlebnis.

Der Markt für ästhetische Medizin und Longevity wächst sehr stark. Gleichzeitig verändern sich die Erwartungen der Kunden: Behandlungen sollen professioneller, zugänglicher und selbstverständlicher werden.

Genau diese Entwicklung treiben wir mit MY HEALTH & BEAUTY aktiv voran.

Aufgaben

Für die nächste Phase unseres Wachstums suchen wir einen Head of Operations, der die operative Entwicklung unserer HEALTH&BEAUTY Lounges verantwortet und gemeinsam mit uns die Grundlage für die nächsten 10, 20 oder 100 Standorte schafft.

Wir suchen ausdrücklich keinen Verwalter bestehender Strukturen.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Strukturen hinterfragt, Schwachstellen erkennt, Lösungen entwickelt und diese konsequent umsetzt.

Jemanden, der strategisch denkt und selbst vor Ort ist, mit Teams arbeitet, Trainings durchführt, Probleme löst und Verantwortung übernimmt.

Deine Verantwortung

Du trägst die operative Gesamtverantwortung für unsere Standorte und entwickelst gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung unsere Operations kontinuierlich weiter.

Leadership & People

Du führst unsere Kollegen und späteren Führungskräfte und sorgst dafür, dass Führung nicht nur auf dem Papier stattfindet, sondern im täglichen Geschäft spürbar ist.

Du entwickelst Mitarbeiter weiter, gibst klares Feedback und schaffst Verantwortlichkeiten.

Du erkennst Leistungsträger frühzeitig, entwickelst sie weiter.

Genauso konsequent gehst du mit Underperformance um.

Du sorgst gemeinsam mit unserem Recruiting Team dafür, dass unsere Standorte jederzeit mit den richtigen Menschen besetzt sind und wir auch bei starkem Wachstum oder Ausfällen unsere personellen Standards halten.

Training & Development

Du entwickelst strukturierte Trainings- und Weiterbildungsprogramme für unsere operativen Teams.

Du führst Trainings selbst durch und entwickelst gleichzeitig Strukturen, mit denen Wissen innerhalb der Organisation skalierbar weitergegeben werden kann.

Du etablierst klare Standards für Onboarding, Führung, Verkauf, Kundenservice und operative Abläufe.

Dabei misst du nicht nur, ob Trainings stattgefunden haben, sondern ob sie tatsächlich zu besserer Performance führen.

Operational Excellence

Du analysierst die operativen Prozesse des Unternehmens und stellst sie kontinuierlich infrage.

Was funktioniert, wird standardisiert.

Was nicht funktioniert, wird verändert.

Was unnötig kompliziert ist, wird vereinfacht.

Du entwickelst SOPs, Verantwortlichkeiten und Prozesse, die für jeden Standort klar verständlich und reproduzierbar sind.

Dein Anspruch ist, dass ein Kunde unabhängig vom Standort ein konstant hohes MY-HEALTH-&-BEAUTY-Erlebnis erhält.

Performance & KPIs

Du definierst gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung die relevanten operativen KPIs und stellst sicher, dass diese verstanden und konsequent gesteuert werden.

Dazu gehören insbesondere Produktivität, Personaleinsatz, Auslastung, Umsatzperformance, Kundenbindung, Servicequalität und operative Effizienz.

Wenn ein Standort seine Ziele verfehlt, analysierst du nicht nur die Zahlen, sondern findest heraus, warum.

Anschließend entwickelst du konkrete Maßnahmen, definierst Verantwortlichkeiten und stellst deren Umsetzung sicher.

Customer Experience & Qualitätsanspruch

Wir wollen nicht durchschnittlich gut sein.

Unser Anspruch ist ein außergewöhnlich hohes Niveau in jedem einzelnen Standort.

Du stellst sicher, dass unsere Standards hinsichtlich Kundenservice, Organisation, Sauberkeit, Auftreten, Kommunikation und operativer Qualität konsequent eingehalten werden.

Du erkennst Abweichungen frühzeitig und greifst ein, bevor aus kleinen Problemen strukturelle Probleme werden.

Dein Ziel ist klar:

Aus 10 erfolgreichen Standorten eine skalierbare, professionelle Operations-Struktur zu bauen, die auch mit weiteren 20, 30 oder 100 Standorten funktioniert.

Qualifikation

Diese Position ist bewusst nicht für jeden geeignet.

Wir suchen einen außergewöhnlich leistungsorientierten Menschen mit einem sehr hohen eigenen Anspruch.

Du solltest bereits bewiesen haben, dass du Menschen führen, operative Strukturen verbessern und Verantwortung für Ergebnisse übernehmen kannst.

Was du zwingend mitbringen solltest

Mehrjährige relevante Führungserfahrung in einer anspruchsvollen operativen Organisation.

Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Führung größerer Teams und mehrerer Führungsebenen.

Idealerweise hast du bereits Verantwortung für mehrere Standorte oder dezentrale operative Einheiten getragen.

Du hast Erfahrung darin, Mitarbeiter nicht nur zu verwalten, sondern tatsächlich zu entwickeln, zu motivieren und leistungsfähiger zu machen.

Du kannst professionelle Trainingskonzepte entwickeln und bist gleichzeitig stark genug in Kommunikation und Auftreten, diese Trainings selbst durchzuführen.

Du bist zahlengetrieben und kannst aus KPIs konkrete operative Entscheidungen ableiten.

title: Head of Operations (Zürich, 100%)
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring a Head of Operations


⏰ Start date: ASAP

📍Zürich, Switzerland (on-site, remote not possible)

🦾 Full-time (100%)

Loki Robotics’ mission is to make physical services an abundant commodity for everyone through robotics and physical AI. We build, deploy and operate expert robots with unique capabilities to automate commercial facility services at scale. We believe emergent capabilities in physical AI are unlocked by taking a straight shot to useful, performant robots deployed in the real world. We’re a tight team that takes initiative, operates with agency, and genuinely cares about doing outstanding work.

Your role

Every robot we produce has to be prepared, shipped, deployed, operated, serviced and improved in the field. As Head of Operations, you own that end to end. You are the execution engine that customers and the rest of Loki rely on to make deployments happen, and you build the operations organization that keeps getting better at it: more automated, more productized and spread across more roles and geographies as we scale.

What you will be doing

  • Own deployment implementation: site assessments, customer kick-offs, onsite supervision, staff training, performance assessment and all customer communication along the way

  • Run logistics for every deployment: fulfillment, shipping, import/export, compliance and coordination with the customer’s receiving side

  • Build and run the operations organization: SOPs, scheduling, allocating operator bandwidth across deployments, testing and internal data collection, among others

  • Work with our testing engineers on release, performance and quality assurance testing: reporting procedures, schedules and the bandwidth to execute them

  • Relay what customers and field operations tell you back to product, GTM and R&D

  • Find operations bottlenecks and remove them, whether through a new process, a new hire, a change in structure or by killing a process entirely. Many ops tasks exist because a feature is missing or because that is how it has always been done. Your job is to delete, automate or productize them

  • Hire, onboard and lead the operations team: define roles, onboarding, incentives, internal assessments and the KPIs that steer our operations organization

  • Train partner operators and distributors in deployment operations as we expand

What you should have

  • 5+ years in operations, field deployment, implementation or a comparable role combining management and execution-heavy tasks. You have managed teams for a meaningful part of that experience

  • You have built an operations function at an early-stage company from the ground up, without a support structure already in place for you to consume

  • You have deployed physical products at customer sites: hardware, robotics, automation or industrial equipment. Robotics or facility services is a strong plus

  • You operate across both horizons at once: what has to happen in the next 12 hours and what the org needs to look like in 3 months. You know at any moment what the top priority is and what to delegate

  • You are hands-on. An undefined process, a missing checklist or one overworked colleague is enough for you to act, fixing it for tomorrow and making sure it does not come back

  • You are the best manager in the room. You set clear goals, put people where their strengths accelerate the team and get along with people from all walks of life.

  • You are detail-oriented and think from first principles, and you can turn that into clear, robust processes that others can just follow

  • You take action on a goal without waiting for direction, and ask for help when you need it without letting that block you

  • Excellent communication in English

What we offer

  • Ownership of Loki’s deployment, internal operations and field ops end-to-end

  • The opportunity to build and lead the operations org as we scale across geographies

  • Close partnership with the founders/leadership team

  • Flat hierarchy, quick decision making and real responsibility in executing Loki’s global expansion

  • Be at the forefront of changing how physical services are delivered

Don’t worry if you don’t hit every checkmark. We value people who learn fast and care about building great products. If Loki excites you and you believe you can help us scale, just give it a go and apply.


At Loki, you are accepted for who you are. We welcome applicants of every background, gender, age and nationality. Different experiences and perspectives make our team and our product better.

title: Head of Product (Flex)
descriptionHtml:
Head of Product 

  • Location: London (Hybrid Office - 3+ days per week)

  • Salary: £112,000 - £140,000

  • Team: Product (Flex)

  • Level: HoD

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do

As Head of Product for Flex, you own the vision, strategy and commercial success of our residential VPP platform globally. You lead a product organisation of Product Managers embedded across our device integration, optimisation, monetisation and SaaS platform teams, and you sit on the Flex Leadership team alongside our Head of Engineering, jointly accountable for the performance of the whole Flex business. Specifically, you will:

  • Set and own the global product strategy for Flex, translating Kaluza's company-level strategy into a roadmap spanning device integrations, multi-asset optimisation (EV, battery, solar, HEMS), monetisation and market access, and self-serve SaaS capabilities.

  • Build and lead a high-performing product organisation - hiring, developing and retaining Product Managers of all levels, and identifying and growing the next generation of product leaders within Flex.

  • Make the trade-off calls that matter: balance the needs of our two core client segments - energy retailers and device OEMs - defaulting to retailer priorities where they conflict, in line with Flex's strategy, while protecting the long-term health of the platform.

  • Partner closely with the Head of Engineering and our Commercial and Partnerships teams to align product, technical and commercial strategy, and to make resourcing and investment decisions across Flex's product and engineering teams.

  • Define annual goals and OKRs for Flex, aligned to Kaluza's company strategy, and hold your organisation accountable for delivering measurable commercial and platform-quality outcomes.

  • Be the client-facing expert for Flex product: lead demos and pitches for prospective retailer and OEM clients, contribute to proposals and pricing, and represent Flex's product practice at Kaluza-wide and industry forums.

  • Own the long-term roadmap narrative - kept current, accessible, and able to be told confidently to prospects and clients two years out - as well as internally to engineering, design, partnerships and commercial teams.

  • Build and maintain your network with Product, Partnership, Engineering and Commercial leaders across Kaluza, ensuring insight from Flex feeds into - and benefits from - the wider Kaluza product strategy.

  • Champion product craft and ways of working across Flex, raising the bar for discovery, prioritisation and measurable impact, in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment where judgement on trade-offs matters as much as vision.

What you’ll bring 

Ideally you’ll have/be

  • Be a proven, experienced product leader with a track record of building, leading and developing product teams and people managers, not just individual contributors.

  • Be a seasoned expert in product strategy and execution across the full product lifecycle, with a track record of translating ambiguous, complex problems into a clear strategy and roadmap.

  • Have strong commercial instincts - comfortable owning pricing input, business cases and ROI, and able to demonstrate commercial impact and business growth through your teams.

  • Be an excellent communicator, able to present complex, ambiguous problems clearly and persuasively to technical and non-technical audiences, from engineers to clients to Kaluza's leadership team.

  • Have deep experience with, or a genuine ability to quickly get up to speed in, complex multi-sided B2B / B2B2C technology platforms - direct experience in energy, DER orchestration, IoT device platforms or smart devices is a strong plus.

  • Be comfortable operating with high ambiguity, making the call yourself where appropriate and knowing when to escalate, in a fast-paced and frequently changing environment.

  • Have a track record of fostering a strong product culture and coaching others - including peers without being their formal manager - to raise the standard of product work around them.

  • Be data-driven in how you measure impact, and able to hold yourself and your teams accountable to outcomes, not just outputs.

What will set you apart 

  • Experience in energy trading, national and regional flexibility markets, or other VPP monetisation opportunity spaces (e.g. balancing markets, capacity markets, wholesale/imbalance trading, ancillary services).

  • Direct experience with VPPs, EV/battery smart charging, HEMS, or residential demand-flexibility products.

  • Familiarity with UK and/or international energy market mechanics (e.g. BSC, NEM, market settlement, DER integration standards).

  • Experience selling or supporting the sale of platform/SaaS propositions to enterprise clients.

Where you'll work
We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Head of Talent Acquisition
descriptionHtml:
At Joko, our mission is to we help consumers save time and money when shopping online or in-store.

Founded in Paris, Joko is a tech company and certified B Corp with over 120 talents across Paris, Barcelona, and New York (and beyond). More than 7 million users already save money every day at 10,000+ merchants with Joko.

From cashback and automatic coupons to price alerts, we've kept expanding our products to make shopping smarter. Today, Joko is an AI shopping app: with Juno, our shopping assistant, users can find the right product at the best price in only a few seconds, with recommendations that get sharper the more they use it.

Having reached profitability in our core market, we’re now scaling globally, with a strong focus on the US.

It’s still day 1, come build the future of shopping with us!

🧲 Our Talent Team

At Joko, hiring has been a founding obsession since day one. Our founders have always been convinced that markets aren't cracked with headcount — they're cracked with talent density. That bet has worked: we've grown to 6 million users and become one of France's most recognized shopping apps with just 30 people in the early years, and we've kept the same bar as we've scaled past 100.

The Talent team exists because we believe talent is the single biggest asset of a company, and that identifying, attracting, and closing the best profiles is a craft worth investing in seriously. We are constantly experimenting with state-of-the-art techniques, tools, and processes to find the people who will build the future of shopping with us.

Today, the Talent team sits within the broader People function, which also covers People Ops, People Business Partnering, and Workplace across France, Spain, and our growing international footprint into the US. We are a team with a big scope and rare ownership per person, and we move fast.

✨ Why this role is special

Recruiting is Joko's #1 company objective — because talent unlocks everything else — which makes this one of the most strategic seats in the company. Three things make it genuinely rare:

  • The team is exceptionally involved in hiring. From ICs to managers to founders, recruiting is treated as a first-class responsibility, not something delegated to TA. You will work with hiring partners who actually show up, give sharp feedback, and care about the bar as much as you do.

  • You will have the tools, and the budget, to be on the frontier. We already work with a modern stack (Ashby, Claude, Claap, and more), and we keep investing to stay among the most performant and modern TA setups out there. You will not be fighting for basic tooling, you will be deciding what comes next.

  • You will live a genuinely unique scale moment. Growing from 100+ people today to 200+ within 18 months, with a real international component (France, Spain, US, and more to come) is the kind of stretch many TA leaders don’t often get to experience. You get to do it here, with a company that has already proven it can build a recognized product with a fraction of the usual headcount.

To be concrete about what this looks like in practice: in year one, the job is to build the team — sourcing, hiring, and coaching the TAMs who will power Joko's growth. The AI strategy, international employer brand, and long-term function design are the horizon you are building toward. They are real, and you will own them fully. But the foundation comes first, and the foundation is the team.

🎯 What you will do

As Head of Talent Acquisition, your mission is to build and lead the TA function that will take Joko from 100+ people today to 200+ within 18 months, and beyond, with the bar, craft, and intentionality that have defined Joko's talent density since day one. You will report to the VP People and be part of the People leadership team, alongside the Head of People Operations and our Lead People Business Partner. You will partner closely with founders, hiring managers, and the broader People team.

  • Build and own the TA team: The most important thing you will do, especially early on, is hire the recruiters who will hire everyone else. Two Talent Acquisition Managers are already in the team, and four more TAM positions are open today. You will make the case for what else the function needs over time, from sourcing specialization onward, and recruit, coach, and grow the team around you.

  • Define how Joko recruits: Inbound, outbound, RPO management, agency relationships, tooling (Ashby), and process are all yours. You will set the standards, not just execute against them — including upskilling hiring managers so the bar is applied consistently across every panel.

  • Recruit senior and critical roles yourself: You will stay close to the hardest hires. You know when to delegate and when to own the desk.

  • Build a global AI strategy for recruiting: The way recruiting is done is changing drastically with AI. You will define and roll out Joko's AI strategy for TA: which parts of the funnel to automate, which tools to deploy, how to keep human judgment where it matters most, and how to turn AI into a real competitive advantage in how we source, screen, and close. You will own this end to end.

  • Drive an international employer brand: We are not well known enough yet, and that is costing us. You will build an employer brand strategy that reflects who we actually are, starting in France, scaling very soon to Spain, and preparing for the US and other markets.

👀 Who we're looking for

  • Experience: You have stood up a TA function before, or rebuilt one, and you have also worked somewhere with best-in-class standards. You can operate in both 0-to-1 mode and best-in-class mode, and you know when to switch. The strongest candidate may not have done "just" Talent — a track record that spans ops, sales, consulting, or building things beyond recruiting is a real asset here.

  • Coaching mindset: You know how to develop the resourcefulness and drive of the people you manage. You see growing recruiters as part of the job, not a tax on it.

  • High-bar mindset: Joko's culture is built on talent density. Our hiring managers are involved, exacting, and not afraid to pass on a 90% candidate. You find that energizing, not frustrating.

  • Ops-oriented and performance-driven: You think in systems, not one-offs. You instrument the funnel, care about the numbers, and build process that holds up as the team scales.

  • Strong sense of craft in TA: You know the difference between a recruiter who has relied on inbound for years and one who genuinely knows how to source. You’ve done both, and you know which approach each situation calls for.

  • Analytical skills: You reason with data — funnel metrics, conversion rates, capacity plans — and you use it to drive decisions, not to decorate slides.

  • Attention to detail: You know candidates judge us on every touchpoint — an outreach message, a scorecard, an offer letter — and you hold the bar on all of them.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. You take ownership without being asked, you welcome feedback, and you go the extra mile by default.

  • Curious and experimental about AI: You don't claim to have it all figured out, the field moves too fast for that. But you have hands-on experience deploying AI tools into a TA function, you have strong opinions formed from real attempts (and real failures), and you genuinely enjoy figuring out what works.

  • International scope: Paris, Barcelona, New York, our footprint is growing. You are comfortable recruiting across geographies and building an Employee Value Proposition that resonates in more than one market.

  • Location: Based in Paris.

  • Education: No specific requirement. Track record matters more than credentials.

  • Languages: You are fluent in French and English (our working language). Spanish is a plus.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

  • 💸 Top-market compensation

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

  • 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

  • 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

  • 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

  • …and much more, check the full list here!

🤝 Our hiring process

  1. Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

  2. Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

  3. Step 2 – Role-specific assessments

    • For non-engineering roles: A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

    • For engineering roles: A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

  4. Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

  5. References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

☕ You may also be invited for coffee with team members to get a feel for our culture.

Compensation: €79K – €114K • Offers Equity

descriptionHtml:
About the Role:

Reporting into the Brand Marketing Director, we’re looking for a Head of VIP, Influencers & PR to build TALA’s profile, cultural relevance and desirability through the people, partnerships, moments and conversations that matter.

You’ll lead the strategy across VIP partnerships, Influencers, Ambassadors, Pro, PR, gifting and events, turning TALA into a brand that people see, talk about and want to be part of.

You’ll know and understand that the fastest way to build awareness is to put TALA in the right hands, in the right places, with the right people.

The successful candidate will bring a serious black book of relevant VIPs from celebrities and musicians to stylists, athletes, creators and cultural tastemakers and know how to build genuine relationships with them.

You’ll be responsible for creating the moments that make TALA feel bigger, more culturally relevant and impossible to ignore.

Tasks

What You’ll Own

VIP & Cultural Partnerships

  • Build and own TALA’s VIP strategy, identifying the people who can meaningfully increase awareness, desirability and cultural relevance.
  • Develop relationships with celebrities, musicians, stylists, athletes, tastemakers and influential cultural figures.
  • Bring a strong existing network and continually build TALA’s VIP black book.
  • Create strategic partnerships that go beyond gifting from organic product placement to collaborations, appearances and brand moments.
  • Ensure TALA is consistently seen on the right people, in the right places and at the right cultural moments.

Ambassador & Pro Programmes

  • Own the strategy, vision and evolution of TALA’s Ambassador and Pro programmes.
  • Define the role these programmes play within TALA’s broader brand and awareness strategy, including who we want to attract, why they matter and what we want them to deliver.
  • Establish the programme proposition, structure, tiers, criteria and long-term growth strategy.
  • Together with the team, build a best-in-class network of ambassadors and professional athletes who genuinely align with TALA and can become powerful advocates for the brand.
  • Set the strategic direction for recruitment, relationship development, activation and retention, with the team responsible for day-to-day programme management and execution.
  • Continuously assess and evolve the programmes based on KPIs including brand impact, reach, engagement and commercial contribution.

Influencer

  • Own the overall influencer strategy, defining how influencer partnerships drive awareness, cultural relevance, desirability and growth.
  • Set the direction for the talent TALA works with, from high-profile creators and cultural tastemakers to emerging talent and community voices.
  • Identify opportunities to move beyond traditional influencer activity into cultural partnerships, organic product placement and high-impact moments.
  • Ensure influencer strategy is integrated with VIP, Ambassador, Pro, PR, gifting, social and campaign activity.
  • Set clear KPIs and continuously evolve the strategy based on performance and cultural opportunity.

Gifting

  • Own the strategic direction for TALA gifting, transforming it from a reactive PR function into a significant awareness and brand-building engine.
  • Together with the team, define who TALA should be gifting, when, why and what we want gifting to achieve.
  • Oversee the strategy for key product launches, cultural moments, VIP gifting, stylist seeding and wider brand moments.
  • Lead the team in developing, signing off and executing gifting programmes, ensuring activity ladders back to wider brand and campaign priorities.

PR

  • Together with the Brand Marketing Director own the overall PR strategy and communications agenda for TALA.
  • Define the role of PR within the wider brand strategy and how it will contribute to building fame, credibility and awareness.
  • Set the annual PR strategy, priorities, narratives and key cultural moments, working closely with Brand Marketing, Social, Influencer and Product.
  • Brief the PR agency to establish the types of stories TALA should be known for and proactively identify opportunities to create news rather than simply respond to it.
  • Ensure the PR team and agency has a clear roadmap and empower them to execute against it.

Events & Experiences

  • Own the TALA events and experiences strategy, defining how physical brand experiences can drive awareness, desirability, community and growth.
  • Set the annual events strategy, including the role of VIP events, consumer experiences, cultural moments, product launches, retail activations and larger-scale brand moments.
  • Define what makes a TALA experience distinctive and ensure every activation is rooted in the brand and designed to generate impact beyond the room.
  • Identify and feed into the events team opportunities for TALA to create culturally relevant moments that can extend into PR, social and organic conversation.
  • Oversee the brief and objectives for key events, with the team responsible for planning and delivering the experience.
  • Oversee the evaluation of the effectiveness of events against awareness, reach, brand impact and commercial objectives, continually evolving the approach.

Requirements

About You

We’re looking for someone who is highly connected, culturally switched-on and relentlessly ambitious.

You will likely have:

  • Significant experience across VIP, celebrity, influencers, PR and events within fashion, beauty, lifestyle or a culturally relevant consumer brand.
  • A strong existing network of VIPs, stylists, agents, managers, media and cultural tastemakers.
  • A proven ability to build authentic relationships with high-profile talent.
  • Experience creating campaigns and moments that generate significant awareness and organic conversation.
  • Strong commercial and strategic thinking, understanding that awareness must ultimately contribute to brand and business growth.
  • A strong understanding of culture, fashion, music, TV, sport, entertainment and what makes people talk.
  • An instinct for what feels cool, relevant and TALA.
  • Exceptional relationship-building and negotiation skills.
  • The confidence to challenge the status quo and create ideas that haven't been done before.
  • A highly proactive, entrepreneurial approach, you’ll spot opportunities rather than wait for a brief.
  • The ability to operate at both strategic and executional level, from defining the annual VIP strategy to picking up the phone to a stylist.

What Success Looks Like

You’ll know you’re succeeding when:

  • TALA is increasingly seen on the right people.
  • We have a strong and growing network of A-list and culturally relevant VIPs who genuinely want to wear and engage with TALA.
  • TALA becomes a brand that celebrities, stylists and cultural tastemakers actively want to be associated with.
  • Our Ambassador and Pro programmes become recognised as some of the most exciting programmes in the category.
  • Gifting creates genuine organic reach, conversation and product desire.
  • Our events become moments people want to attend and talk about.
  • TALA earns more high-quality PR and cultural coverage.
  • We create moments that travel across social, PR and culture, delivering awareness well beyond the original activation.
  • Most importantly, you help move TALA from a brand people discover on social media to a brand people know, recognise and want.

Benefits

What we can offer:

  • 25 days holiday a year plus bank holidays
  • Very generous employee discount after probation period
  • Nominated Friends & Family Discount
  • Clothing allowance spending gift
  • Class Pass or Gym Flex membership
  • Health Shield
  • Enhanced maternity/paternity pay
  • Charity fundraising match of up to £1,000

About us:

TALA is an activewear brand built to actively solve problems without creating new ones for people, the planet, or anyone else. Every collection prioritises functionality and thoughtful design, combining premium fabrics with multi-way versatility and flattering fits that deliver maximum impact with minimal effort. Each piece is crafted with attention to detail, ensuring women can look and feel their best with ease.

When founder Grace Beverley shifted from fast fashion to more sustainable options in her everyday clothing, she found a host of responsibly made options in every category other than activewear. Founding TALA in 2019, the proud female-led brand is on a mission to make consciously made active and off-duty styles accessible and inclusive without sacrificing performance or fit.

title: IAM Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
As an IAM Software Engineer, you’ll focus on Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) solutions. Your work combines technical analysis, platform configuration, low-code implementation, integration, testing, and troubleshooting, with custom coding where needed. You’ll work closely with engineers, architects, consultants, and customer teams to deliver secure, reliable solutions. 

You’ll join an engineering delivery team of around 8–12 people, working across customer assignments in two-week sprints, often with a specific sprint focus. Our ‘you build it, you run it’ approach combines implementation, ongoing improvement, and troubleshooting after delivery, supported by senior engineers in your own and neighbouring teams doing similar work. 

What you’ll do as an IAM Software Engineer 

  • Design and deliver IGA solutions that help customers govern access, using standard platform capabilities, low-code tools, and integration standards, with C#, SQL, and APIs where needed. 
  • Translate customer needs into technical designs and engineering tasks, working with architects, security engineers, and customer stakeholders to meet security, compliance, scalability, and maintainability requirements. 
  • Troubleshoot complex IAM issues, identify root causes, and implement lasting improvements that reduce recurrence and security risk. 
  • Improve automation and delivery practices, using PowerShell and CI/CD where appropriate to make implementation and ongoing changes more reliable. 
  • Share knowledge and support junior engineers through mentoring, design sessions, and reviews of configurations, integrations, and code. 

The impact you’ll have 

Your engineering work will help leading organizations manage access confidently, protect sensitive data, and comply with evolving regulations. By building reliable IAM solutions and improving delivery practices, you’ll contribute to technical strategy and help the team deliver more effectively—strengthening client security and trust in the digital landscape. 

What we can offer you 

Autonomy in your work and support for your career development. 

  • Permanent, full-time contract (40 hours per week) 
  • Flexible, hybrid working: typically two days per week on location—one at a client site and one at our Waardenburg office. 
  • Work outside normal hours is rare (currently fewer than five occasions per year) and always discussed in advance. 
  • Typically, 5–15 learning days per year for your development, including certifications and events. Training and associated costs are agreed individually rather than through a fixed training budget. 
  • 30 days of annual leave: 25 flexible days and 5 fixed company days. 
  • Variable team bonus and annual profit distribution 
  • Mobility budget or company lease car 
  • Private pension scheme 
  • Home office setup budget and monthly remote work allowance 
  • Regular team and company social events 

What you’ll bring to the team 

Core experience and skills 

  • 3–6 years in software or platform engineering, including at least one year designing and implementing IGA solutions such as Omada Identity or Microsoft Entra ID Governance. 
  • Experience in solution design, configuration, API integration, testing, and deployment, using Git and CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Azure DevOps). 
  • Practical C# and SQL experience to troubleshoot and extend IAM solutions where needed. 
  • Strong analytical, design, and problem-solving skills, with a deep understanding of software security and the ability to turn security and compliance requirements into practical solutions. 
  • A relevant bachelor’s degree (e.g., computer science or information security), or equivalent experience. 

How you work 

  • Strong collaboration, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with a structured, proactive approach and the ability to drive work independently. 

Practical requirements 

  • English at C1 and Dutch at B2 or higher, written and spoken. 
  • Client-site travel is within the Netherlands, with current major clients in the Randstad. You’re able and willing to travel to those sites and our Waardenburg office; no driver’s license is required. 
  • Currently residing in the Netherlands and eligible to work here. 

Nice to have 

  • Azure experience. 
  • AI-assisted tools for analysis, configuration, testing, documentation, or coding. 
  • Relevant certifications, e.g., Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate, Omada Certified Engineer, or CISSP. 

About SITS | Traxion 

SITS | Traxion specializes in Identity & Access Management, with 24 years of consulting experience and a team of 120 specialists. We work with organizations across sectors, including Schiphol Group, dsm-firmenich, Gemeente Rotterdam, Belastingdienst, E.ON, and Ayvens. 

As part of the European IT security group SITS, we combine international collaboration with a flat organizational structure and a respectful, collaborative culture. 

Ready to make an impact and secure Europe’s digital identities? Apply today!

At SITS | Traxion, we believe diversity strengthens our teams and fosters innovation. We are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone, regardless of gender, background, or experience, can thrive.

title: Identity & Access Management Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Who is Sonar?

Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence.

Position description

We are looking for an experienced Identity & Access Management (IAM) Engineer to design, build, and operate the identity platforms that secure access to our applications, infrastructure, and data. You will own the technical direction of our IAM ecosystem, including authentication, authorization, lifecycle management, and privileged access. You will work with security, IT, engineering, and compliance teams to deliver a secure, scalable, and user-friendly access experience aligned with Zero Trust principles.


What you will do

  • Design, implement, and maintain enterprise IAM solutions, including SSO, MFA, federation, and directory services.

  • Architect and manage identity lifecycle processes (joiner/mover/leaver), automating provisioning and deprovisioning across SaaS, cloud, and on-prem systems.

  • Implement and operate Privileged Access Management (PAM), including vaulting, session management, and just-in-time access.

  • Lead Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) initiatives such as access reviews, certifications, role-based access control (RBAC), and segregation-of-duties controls.

  • Integrate applications with the identity platform using SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, SCIM, and LDAP.

  • Develop automation and tooling (APIs, scripts, CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code) to reduce manual identity operations.

  • Secure cloud identity and access across AWS, Azure, and/or GCP, including IAM policies, workload identity, and service accounts.

  • Define and enforce authentication and authorization standards, policies, and best practices.

  • Monitor identity-related threats and support detection and response for account compromise, credential abuse, and privilege escalation.


Experience and qualifications

  • 6 to 15 years of experience in IAM, security engineering, or a related field.

  • Hands-on experience with at least one major IAM platform such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Ping Identity, ForgeRock, SailPoint, or CyberArk.

  • Strong knowledge of identity protocols and standards: SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SCIM, LDAP, and Kerberos.

  • Experience with Active Directory and directory services architecture.

  • Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language (Python, PowerShell, Go, Java, or JavaScript).

  • Solid understanding of cloud IAM models (AWS IAM, Azure RBAC, GCP IAM).

  • Experience with MFA, passwordless, and conditional or risk-based access.

  • Familiarity with Zero Trust, least privilege, and defense-in-depth principles.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Additional comments

This role is based in Geneva. We are unable to consider candidates unwilling to be in Geneva, but we are willing to relocate the right candidate.

We value diversity, equity, and inclusion

At Sonar, we believe that our diversity is our strength. We are a global company that values and respects different backgrounds, perspectives, and cultures. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their best. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome all qualified applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

If you need any accommodation, please reach out to us at All offers of employment at Sonar are contingent upon the results of a comprehensive background check and reference verification conducted before the start date.

Applications that are submitted through agencies or third party recruiters will not be considered.

title: Information Architects
descriptionHtml:
Information Architect

Permanent | Hybrid | Data Architecture | Enterprise Architecture

The Role:

We are seeking an experienced Information Data Architect to design, develop and evolve information architecture across complex enterprise environments. This role will play a key part in shaping data models, improving architecture design and ensuring information solutions align with wider business and enterprise architecture strategies. Working closely with stakeholders, architects and technical teams, you will influence critical design decisions and drive improvements in how information is structured, governed and utilised across the organisation.

You'll join a data-driven environment where information is recognised as a strategic asset. Working with advanced data platforms, business systems and enterprise architecture tools, you will support the development of robust data foundations that enable smarter decision-making and long-term organisational success. This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to enterprise-wide data and information architecture whilst helping shape future data strategy and standards.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain conceptual, logical and physical data models across multiple business domains.
  • Collaborate with enterprise architects, technical teams and business stakeholders to ensure data solutions meet strategic, technical and operational requirements.
  • Support data integration initiatives and information flows, ensuring consistency, quality and interoperability across systems.
  • Define and apply data architecture standards, frameworks and best practices across the organisation.
  • Provide expert guidance on data architecture approaches, principles and governance.
  • Support information architecture activities that enable scalable, reusable and maintainable data solutions.
  • Contribute to enterprise architecture initiatives, ensuring data architecture aligns with wider technology and business strategies.
  • Produce architecture documentation, models and artefacts using recognised architecture repositories and tooling.
  • Participate in design reviews, governance forums and architecture assurance activities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve data quality, accessibility, consistency and reuse across the enterprise.

Skills & Experience:

  • Extensive experience across data architecture disciplines, including conceptual, logical and physical data modelling.
  • Experience applying one or more recognised data architecture modelling approaches or notations such as ArchiMate, SysML, UML, XML or XSLT.
  • Strong understanding of system integration, relational databases, interface design and data structures.
  • Proven experience developing scalable data models and information architecture solutions using recognised architecture repositories such as BizzDesign, Sparx EA or similar.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to present complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, applying structured thinking to business and technical challenges.
  • Experience using recognised external data architecture standards and frameworks, including ISO, BSI, ASD S-Series, OAGi or equivalent.
  • Experience working within complex enterprise environments with multiple stakeholders and interconnected systems.

Desirable Skills:

  • Knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks and methodologies.
  • Experience supporting enterprise data governance and information management initiatives.
  • Understanding of modern data platforms, analytics ecosystems and cloud-based data technologies.
  • Experience working within highly regulated sectors such as defence, aerospace, government or critical national infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with Agile delivery methodologies and cross-functional teams.

The successful candidate will deliver robust, scalable and well-governed information architecture that supports both business objectives and enterprise strategy. They will establish clear data standards, improve consistency and integration across systems, and ensure data assets are structured to support future growth and innovation. Success will be measured through the delivery of high-quality architecture outcomes, improved data accessibility and governance, and the effective adoption of enterprise-wide data architecture principles.

title: Integration Architect
descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Position Summary

The Integration Architect is an individual contributor within Metrea's Platform Development Capability Area, owning the architecture, development, and support of system interfaces across the organisation's core ERP, Supply Chain, and Maintenance business applications. Drawing on strong .NET, API/SFTP integration, conversion scripting, and SQL development experience, the postholder will design and deliver the interfaces and custom system features that connect Metrea's business-critical platforms. 

The role calls for a strong technical background coupled with a solid understanding of business process, and the ability to interact effectively with personnel at all levels of the business. In an entrepreneurial and fast-paced environment, there will be a need to adapt and rapidly prioritise to changing business needs in support of the company's commercial and operational objectives. 

This is a hands-on architecture and development role. The successful candidate will be expected to design solutions, build integrations, develop custom code and scripts, troubleshoot issues, and engage directly with business stakeholders.

What You'll Do

  • Participate in project planning activities, especially as it relates to scoping new system implementation initiatives  
  • Work closely with project team and end users, in order to gather information specific to interfaces, conversions, and enhancement needs  
  • Creation of technical specifications  
  • Table/field level mapping between systems required to develop interfaces and conversion scripts  
  • Development and support of interfaces (including APIs and SFTP file transfers) between our ERP system and aircraft flight operations, logistics, and maintenance systems, along with integrations with third party solutions  
  • Development of conversion scripts, when required  
  • Development of custom code that is scalable and extendable  
  • Development of frameworks and tools to support integrations and conversions  
  • Daily monitoring of system interfaces  
  • Debugging production issues  

What You Bring

  • Self-motivated; team oriented; responsible, and reliable    
  • Positive attitude and proactive style. Candidate must have the ability to work in a structured, yet variable environment  
  • Expertise in interface architecture and development include API development (Rest/JSON and SOAP/XML), and flat file transfers via SFTP  
  • Experience with integration and ETL frameworks
